channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Digital ID at TSA explained: Apple Wallet, Google Wallet, state apps
item.description: You can show a digital ID on your phone at TSA checkpoints in more than 250 US airports, by tapping the reader or scanning a QR code, but TSA still wants every traveler to carry a physical ID as well.

item.title: iPhone Duo fold test explained: how many folds the hinge can take
item.description: CNET's folding machine passed 451,000 folds on the iPhone Duo by 13 November with the phone still working but the hinge loosening, while Apple hasn't published a fold rating of its own.

item.title: Parental controls on iPhone vs Android: setting up a kid's phone
item.description: On an iPhone, parental controls come from a Child Account in Family Sharing and Screen Time; on Android, from Google's Family Link, and Family Link can't supervise an iPhone, so the child's phone decides which system you use.

item.title: Untitled Starry Sky AI art app turns sketches and photos into art
item.description: Untitled Starry Sky is a free iPhone and iPad app that turns a written idea, a photo or a few drawn strokes into a collage, geometric or abstract painting with AI. It was #60 among free Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Weathercloud app for iPhone shows live weather from real stations
item.description: Weathercloud Network is a free iPhone app that shows live readings from more than 150,000 weather stations around the world, run by professionals and hobbyists. It was #70 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots to keep Siri AI and Gemini out of chats
item.description: Signal now stops screenshots inside its app on iPhone and Android, so AI assistants built into the phone can't read your messages off the screen. On Android it switches on Screen security by itself when it detects an assistant trying to read the screen; on iOS 27 a new Block Siri AI setting does the job.

item.title: Android App Lock won't come to older Android versions, Google says
item.description: Android's built-in App Lock needs a full Android update and can't be added to older versions through Google Play system updates, Google's Mishaal Rahman said on 20 November. Google plans to ship it with Android 17 QPR3 in the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: App Launcher widget for iPhone puts 100+ apps on one home screen page
item.description: App Launcher: Home Screen is a free iPhone and iPad app that turns one full-page widget into a grid of more than 100 app icons, plus two lock screen widgets with eight apps each. It was #89 among free Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Baby tracker app with no subscription: Baby Log & Head Time
item.description: Baby Log & Head Time is a $4.99 one-time iPhone app for logging feedings, naps, diapers, baths and doctor visits with one tap each. It was #42 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Fake Tax Authority app hijacks Android phones, Israel warns
item.description: Israel's National Cyber Directorate warned on 19 November about messages that lead to a fake Google Play page offering a Tax Authority app. Once installed and given permissions, it lets attackers read text messages and one-time codes, turn on the camera and control the phone.

item.title: Frame Pro Camera app: RAW iPhone photos with film-style looks
item.description: Frame: Pro Camera is a $9.99 iPhone camera app that shoots RAW and develops the photos with film-style colour and grain instead of the iPhone's usual processing. It was #77 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: GasSavvy gas price app counts your discounts before ranking stations
item.description: GasSavvy is a new 1.99 dollar iPhone app that ranks nearby gas stations by what a full tank would cost you after the discounts you already have, such as Walmart+, Shell Fuel Rewards, Exxon Mobil Rewards+, T-Mobile Tuesdays, AAA or AARP. It came out on 19 November and was #12 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: GTA 6 cloud gaming explained: Xbox One, PC, Remote Play and size
item.description: GTA 6 came out on 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, Xbox One owners can only stream it through Xbox Cloud Gaming, there's no PC version or PC streaming, and Remote Play lets you stream it from your own console to another screen.

item.title: Hurricane preparedness app Batten Down plans before and after a storm
item.description: Batten Down is a $1.99 iPhone app for families and small businesses that covers getting ready for a hurricane, checking in during one and making insurance claims after. It was #26 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Is it safe to charge your phone at the airport? Juice jacking explained
item.description: Charging from an airport USB port carries a small risk known as juice jacking, where a rigged port tries to reach your phone's data, but security researchers know of no credible real attacks, and your own charger or a battery pack takes the risk away.

item.title: Long exposure on iPhone: Adobe Project Indigo adds a Long mode
item.description: Adobe's free Project Indigo camera app for iPhone now has a separate Long Exposure mode, called Long, next to Photo and Night. It merges many short frames into one picture and shows the result building up live in the viewfinder.

item.title: Meta Muse Chrome extension puts the AI agent in your browser sidebar
item.description: The Muse Chrome extension, Meta's AI agent in Chrome's side panel, is now official: Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang announced it on X on 20 November. Muse chats with you next to any page and can shop, book travel and handle tasks in its own group of tabs.

item.title: On Pace step counter for Apple Watch compares today with your average
item.description: On Pace: Steps vs Average is a new 99-cent step counter that shows on your Apple Watch face and iPhone Home Screen whether you're walking more or less than on a usual day. It was #1 in Health & Fitness among paid apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: Port Things: an offline cruise port guide app for iPhone
item.description: Port Things is a new iPhone and iPad app with offline guides to cruise ports, made by Incmplte L.L.C. It costs $4.99 and was #60 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 20 November.

item.title: SnowBrains app: free ski news, snow forecasts and powder alerts
item.description: SnowBrains News & Weather puts ski and snowboard news and 5- and 7-day snow forecasts for more than 700 resorts in the US and Canada into one free iPhone app. It was #82 in Weather on the US App Store's free chart on 20 November.

item.title: Streaming bundles 2026 explained: Disney+ Hulu app, HBO Max, Fubo
item.description: Streaming services are folding into each other: Hulu's live TV moves into the Disney+ app in December, Paramount+ and HBO Max are due as one bundle in early 2027, and Fubo now adds Disney+ and Hulu to two of its plans at no extra cost.

item.title: Super 909 Drums: free 909-style drum machine app for iPhone and Mac
item.description: AudioKit Pro released Super 909 Drums on 20 November, a free synth-based drum machine modelled on the classic 909 sound, for iPhone, iPad and Mac. The same day it was #65 in Music on the US App Store's free chart.

item.title: Surfshark DNS shutting down on 24 November: switch your DNS servers
item.description: Surfshark is retiring its free public DNS service from 24 November 2026, according to its support page. Anyone who typed its DNS addresses into a phone, computer or router should move to another resolver.

item.title: WhatsApp security update fixes Android bug used in scam messages
item.description: WhatsApp fixed three security flaws, one of which it believes a scammer used: a fake ad-reply message could reveal an Android user's IP address. WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.17.4 had that bug.

item.title: Windows 11 KB5132057 update features: new Search without Edge, new Run
item.description: The optional Windows 11 update KB5132057 brings a rebuilt Search that no longer runs on Edge's web parts, a new Run box you can switch on and a way to turn off the Sticky Keys shortcut. Everyone gets these changes with the 8 December update.

item.title: Android sideloading verification goes worldwide from January 2027
item.description: Google will start requiring a verified developer for Android apps installed from outside the Play Store in every region from January 2027, Ars Technica reports, with the rollout to all devices taking several months. Until now the rule applied only in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand, where it began on 30 September 2026.

item.title: AVANT CAMERA is a cinematic video camera app for iPhone
item.description: AVANT CAMERA adds film-style colour to your videos while you record, so you see the look before you edit. It was #88 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Black Friday scams 2026: fake shops, delivery texts and fake numbers
item.description: The Black Friday scams warned about this month copy real shops, carriers and customer service lines, and going straight to the shop's own app or website and paying by credit card protects against most of them.

item.title: Canva turn off AI features: new switch for free and paid users
item.description: Canva now has a setting that switches off its generative AI tools, such as Magic Expand (which extends a photo), Magic Write and image making in its chatbot. It's there for free and paid accounts, with a second option to see less AI-made content in the library.

item.title: Cryptomator Android 3.0 puts encrypted vaults in the Files app
item.description: Cryptomator's Android app, which encrypts files on your phone before they go to cloud storage, now shows its vaults in Android's Files app and file picker. Other apps can open and save files in a vault directly; version 3.0 is rolling out on Google Play.

item.title: Duolingo event screens: option to skip them coming in December
item.description: Duolingo says it will test a way to skip the event screens that appear after each lesson, such as avatar outfit events, starting with a small group of users next week. A wider rollout is planned for December.

item.title: FernShift shift calendar app for iPhone plans rotating work shifts
item.description: FernShift is a 2.99 dollar iPhone and iPad calendar for people who work rotating shifts, with repeating patterns of up to eight weeks and 12-hour or 8-hour schedules. It was #87 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Gemini for Mac computer use: it now works your apps in the background
item.description: The Gemini app for Mac can now click, type and fill in forms across your Mac's apps, files and websites to finish a task you describe. It's rolling out from 19 November in the US, in English, for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers.

item.title: Google homepage redesign: Gemini sidebar with your chats on desktop
item.description: The Google Search homepage on computers is getting Gemini shortcuts under the search bar for making images, analysing files and brainstorming, in place of the Google Search button. A new sidebar lists your Gemini chats and tasks with a New chat button.

item.title: Halide camera app on iPhone Duo: bigger viewfinder and fill flash
item.description: Halide 3.4, out on 19 November, adds an XL viewfinder for the iPhone Duo when it's open, and can turn the outer screen into a live preview for the person you photograph or into a soft fill light.

item.title: HeyGen Avatar 6: make an AI avatar video of yourself from a photo
item.description: HeyGen launched Avatar 6, a model that turns one photo of you and a short recording of your voice into a video of you reading a script. It makes 2K video, matches hand gestures to what you say and can put two avatars in one conversation.

item.title: HippoMaps: Google Maps alternative where you search in plain words
item.description: HippoMaps is a new open-source map built on OpenStreetMap that understands searches like "pharmacies open now in Bern" or "cafes in Zurich by the Limmat". Its maker showed it on Hacker News on 19 November; it runs in the browser and as an Android app.

item.title: IconSwapper Mac app shows your ChatGPT and Claude usage on Dock icons
item.description: IconSwapper is a new Mac app that changes the icons in your Dock, including live icons that show how much of your ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor allowance you've used and when it resets. It costs 19 dollars once at launch, later 29 dollars.

item.title: Ideogram 4.6 AI image generator edits pictures step by step in 4K
item.description: Ideogram released version 4.6 of its AI image model on 19 November: it makes and edits pictures at up to 4K, and a Precise Edit tool lets you change one part of a picture over several steps, optionally only inside an area you paint. You can also give it up to five reference images.

item.title: Live Tube map in AR: Subwhere shows trains moving under London
item.description: Subwhere AR is a £3.99 app that shows London Underground trains moving below you when you point your phone at the ground. An 18 November update added Paris and Tokyo to Stockholm, and its London view covers all 11 Tube lines from TfL's live arrival predictions.

item.title: LoopListen: shadowing app for iPhone loops a phrase until you get it
item.description: LoopListen is a 99-cent iPhone and iPad app for listening practice: tap A and B to mark a part of a recording, and it repeats that part with pauses so you can say it back. It was #69 among paid Education apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Meta Muse Charm price may be 300 dollars with free Verizon 5G
item.description: Meta plans to sell its Muse Charm, a pocket device for talking to its Muse AI agent, for 300 dollars with up to 12 months of free Verizon 5G data, according to The Information, citing one person familiar with the plans. Meta hasn't confirmed the price or the Verizon offer.

item.title: MoodyRoutine brings Samsung-style Modes and Routines to Pixel phones
item.description: MoodyRoutine is a free Android app that copies the idea of Samsung's Modes and Routines for other phones such as Google Pixels: modes like Sleep or Exercise switch on by time or when headphones connect and change your settings.

item.title: OpenAI phone: Foxconn unit reportedly got an order to build it
item.description: China's Securities Times reports that FIH Mobile, part of iPhone assembler Foxconn, has an order to help build a smartphone for ChatGPT maker OpenAI. The report cites unnamed supply chain sources, and OpenAI hasn't confirmed any phone.

item.title: Passkeys vs passwords explained: how they work on iPhone and Android
item.description: A passkey lets you sign in with your face, fingerprint or phone PIN instead of a password, and because it never leaves your device as a secret you could type in, a fake website can't trick you into handing it over.

item.title: Phone overheating with CarPlay or Android Auto: why and what helps
item.description: A phone running CarPlay or Android Auto often does several heavy jobs at once (navigation, music, mobile data and charging) in a warm car, and Apple and Google both say long navigation sessions, sunlight and hot cars make phones heat up, so a cable, a shaded spot and a lighter load usually help.

item.title: Play That Back camera app: film with live looks on iPhone and Duo
item.description: Play That Back is a new free camera app for iPhone and iPad that shows a colour look live while you film and keeps a clean original of every shot. On the iPhone Duo, the person you're filming sees the look on the outer screen and can pick it.

item.title: Proton Drive import from Google Drive: Easy Switch moves your files
item.description: Proton Drive can now import your Google Drive files and folders through Easy Switch on the web, keeping your folder structure. It's for all plans and rolling out gradually.

item.title: Raylie flight view app shows which side of the plane to sit on
item.description: Raylie is a free iPhone app that turns a boarding pass into a timeline of what you'll see from the window, from sunrise to cities below, and on which side. It was #96 among free Travel apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Running app without subscription: echoRnr costs $9.99 once
item.description: echoRnr is a running app you buy once, with no ads and no monthly fee, and it lets you race a past run of your own or a friend's in real time. It came out on 19 November and was #18 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store the same day.
